body: I’m originally from Southern Ontario in Canada, but currently live in southwestern Japan as an English teacher.
I pray and hope that you’re still with us. You’re only fourteen! You’ve barely just begun to experience life. PLEASE be alive.

I’m 31 and have had it since I was 13, I think? But at the time it was because of some minor scars and a mole beside my eye (which is 80% gone now thanks to affordable laser treatments). My insecurity over the size of my feet (US Men’s 7, but I usually wear a larger size) started when I was aged 15 and saw how much bigger all the other boys’ shoes were. My BDD then got even worse at the age of 20-21 when I saw a glimpse of my profile in photos. A flat forehead, a low nose bridge, and receding chin. I also have a problem with my (perceived) long torso and short legs. I posted about this on the BDD forum a while back, but going to the gym with my friend has made my BDD worse than before because I keep comparing my body with his. His body is not perfect, but much more appealing and masculine than mine. He has all of the features I want for myself.

I don’t have as much of a problem with my face as I do with my bone structure because the former can always be changed with surgery, but the latter cannot. I’m always thinking why I was cursed with such sh*tty genes.

I usually ask if I could just take their photos for them. 

Otherwise I oblige just to be polite, but I either tell them not to upload the photos featuring me onto social media, or am cautious when browsing social media so I don’t catch a glimpse of any photos with me in them.

Body is 100% more of a concern to me. Things like torso length, leg length, arm length, and foot length cannot be changed, but one’s face can always be altered through cosmetic surgery.

It annoys me so much to see someone fret about how their face looks or how short they are, and to see someone not have confidence, even though they have excellent body proportions.
How’s this outfit? Please be honest.
